correctness.rationale: Every Johnson edge extends to a star or top, and any three vertices determine at most one such maximal clique; stars/tops intersect in at most an edge. Within each maximal simplex, pair every face τ of at least three vertices omitting the chosen apex with τ∪{apex} in descending dimension: all >2 simplices collapse, leaving all graph edges and the apex triangles. The hypersimplex Δ(n,k) is convex with Johnson graph 1-skeleton and triangular polygon 2-faces; its boundary dimension n−2≥4 is simply connected, so the cellular two-skeleton (a subcomplex of the flag complex with all edges) kills π1. Thus collapsed complex is simply connected and 2-dimensional. V=C(n,k), E=(1/2)C(n,k)k(n−k), remaining T=C(n,k−1)C(n−k,2)+C(n,k+1)C(k,2); Euler, integral freeness and Hurewicz/Whitehead yield wedge of beta=V−E+T−1 2-spheres. Independent exact counts (6,3):19, (7,3):55, (8,4):181 agree; not an infinite proof.
